title: Saying ‘No’ at Work Can Be Good for Your Health
titleZh: 在工作场合说“不”对你的健康有益
credits: Cathy Bussewitz reported this story for The Associated Press from New York City. Anna Matteo adapted it for VOA Learning English.

sentences.en: From VOA Learning English, this is the Health & Lifestyle report.
sentences.zh: 来自美国之音英语学习频道，这是健康与生活方式报道。

sentences.en: People might find it hard to set work limits or say “no” before taking on too many responsibilities.
sentences.zh: 人们可能很难在工作限度内行事，或在承担过多责任之前说'不'。

sentences.en: But experts say it is important for workers to learn to set such limits, or boundaries.
sentences.zh: 但专家表示，workers学会设定这样的限度或边界很重要。

sentences.en: These limits can be important in helping workers protect their physical and mental health.
sentences.zh: 这些限度在帮助workers保护身心健康方面可能很重要。

sentences.en: And as with any new skill, setting boundaries gets easier with practice.
sentences.zh: 和任何新技能一样，设定边界会随着练习而变得更容易。

sentences.en: Justin Stewart is a 36-year-old who works as a news show production assistant.
sentences.zh: 贾斯汀·斯图尔特是一名36岁的人，担任新闻节目的制作助理。

sentences.en: He told The Associated Press that in the past, he had problems setting clear limits in his work life.
sentences.zh: 他告诉美联社，过去他在工作中难以设定明确的界限。

sentences.en: Stewart explained that when starting his career, he held several jobs.
sentences.zh: 斯图尔特解释说，刚开始职业生涯时，他同时打几份工。

sentences.en: In addition to his full-time position, he also rented cars at the airport and did sales at a store.
sentences.zh: 除了全职工作外，他还在机场租车，并在一家商店做销售。

sentences.en: He said his life was so busy that he said he would sometimes sleep in his car between jobs.
sentences.zh: 他说自己的生活非常忙碌，有时会在两份工作之间睡在车里。

sentences.en: After a time, he had to be hospitalized for extreme tiredness and an infection.
sentences.zh: 过了一段时间后，他因极度疲惫和感染而住院。

sentences.en: Stewart said that over time, his busy work life finally caught up with him.
sentences.zh: 斯图尔特说，随着时间的推移，他繁忙的工作生活终于拖垮了他。

sentences.en: “While people around me praised my hustle, I eventually paid the price.”
sentences.zh: '当我周围的人赞扬我的努力时，我最终付出了代价。'

sentences.en: As a result, Stewart began trying to set boundaries.
sentences.zh: 因此，斯图尔特开始尝试设定界限。

sentences.en: He gave up his side jobs after deciding he could live without the extra money.
sentences.zh: 在决定可以没有额外收入后，他放弃了兼职工作。

sentences.en: If people from the news show contacted him to work after-hours, he told them he was not available and suggested other people who might be able to help.
sentences.zh: 如果新闻节目的人联系他加班，他会告诉他们自己没空，并建议其他可能能帮忙的人。

sentences.en: However, experts say making such changes can be difficult.
sentences.zh: 然而，专家表示，做出这样的改变可能很困难。

sentences.en: Many people already have a hard time turning down work requests –from both co-workers and managers.
sentences.zh: 许多人已经很难拒绝来自同事和经理的工作请求。

sentences.en: For example, it might make some people feel good to be needed or to please others.
sentences.zh: 例如，被需要或取悦他人可能会让一些人感到愉快。

sentences.en: But as with any new skill, setting boundaries can get easier over time.
sentences.zh: 但和任何新技能一样，设定边界会随着时间的推移变得更容易。

sentences.en: Here are some suggestions from employment experts and workers for effectively setting meaningful work limits.
sentences.zh: 以下是就业专家和工作者为有效设定有意义的工作界限所提供的一些建议。

sentences.en: Take control of your time
sentences.zh: 掌控你的时间

sentences.en: If your goal is to do less, adding things to your daily plans may seem like a bad idea.
sentences.zh: 如果你的目标是做得更少，在每日计划中添加事项似乎是个坏主意。

sentences.en: But it can actually provide more control over your time.
sentences.zh: 但它实际上能让你更好地掌控自己的时间。

sentences.en: Bobby Dutton is the founder of event production company GBM6.
sentences.zh: 博比·达顿是活动制作公司 GBM6 的创始人。

sentences.en: Every Monday at 2 p.m., he plans the task he is most likely to delay finishing.
sentences.zh: 每周一下午 2 点，他会规划自己最可能拖延完成的任务。

sentences.en: And to keep from becoming too busy, he even sets his daily activities, like walking his dog and eating lunch.
sentences.zh: 为了避免变得过于忙碌，他甚至安排好自己的日常活动，比如遛狗和吃午饭。

sentences.en: Practice “no” responses
sentences.zh: 练习说“不”

sentences.en: If workers have a hard time saying no, they can write down what to say beforehand.
sentences.zh: 如果工友们难以开口拒绝，他们可以事先写下要说的话。

sentences.en: And it can also help to say it out loud.
sentences.zh: 大声说出来也会有帮助。

sentences.en: Cara Houser is a workplace engagement coach.
sentences.zh: 卡拉·豪瑟是一名职场参与度教练。

sentences.en: She says workers do not always have to explain themselves when turning down a request.
sentences.zh: 她说，工人在拒绝请求时并不总是需要解释原因。

sentences.en: They can simply explain they are not available, thank the person for asking, and suggest when they might be available.
sentences.zh: 他们只需说明自己没有时间，感谢对方的邀请，并建议自己可能什么时候有空。

sentences.en: Amber Krasinski grew up in a working-class environment where saying "no" to a manager could mean losing pay.
sentences.zh: 安伯·克拉辛斯基在一个工人阶级环境中长大，对经理说“不”可能意味着失去收入。

sentences.en: As the founder of marketing company IvyHill Strategies, Krasinski worries that she will lose business if she turns down a project.
sentences.zh: 作为营销公司常春藤战略的创始人，克拉辛担心中自己拒绝某个项目时会失去业务。

sentences.en: So, she often says “not yet” when one more project is too much.
sentences.zh: 所以，当一个项目再多一个就难以承受时，她常常会说“还没到时候”。

sentences.en: “That phrase has helped me through a lot of situations,” she said.
sentences.zh: “这句话帮我度过了很多处境，”她说。

sentences.en: Know yourself
sentences.zh: 了解自己

sentences.en: When asked for help, workers may want to agree immediately.
sentences.zh: 当被请求帮助时，工人可能想立即答应。

sentences.en: However, when faced with a new work request, it can be better to take time before answering.
sentences.zh: 然而，面对新的工作请求时，先花时间再作答可能会更好。

sentences.en: Use the time to consider such things as workload, energy level, and interest.
sentences.zh: 利用这段时间考虑一下工作量、精力水平和兴趣之类的事情。

sentences.en: Israa Nasir is a psychotherapist in New York.
sentences.zh: 伊斯拉·纳西尔是纽约的一名心理治疗师。

sentences.en: She suggests that workers pay attention to the activities and interactions that leave them feeling tired or stressed.
sentences.zh: 她建议员工留意那些让他们感到疲惫或压力的活动和交往。

sentences.en: Those kinds of events can be put on a “No List” to be dealt with later.
sentences.zh: 这类事情可以列入“不做清单”，留待日后处理。

sentences.en: Technology can help
sentences.zh: 技术可以提供帮助

sentences.en: Experts say that just because mobile devices can keep people connected to work all the time, they do not have to interfere with a person’s non-working life.
sentences.zh: 专家表示，仅仅因为移动设备能够让人们随时与工作保持联系，并不意味着它们一定会干扰个人的非工作时间。

sentences.en: For example, Nasir said she found herself checking email far too often on weekends.
sentences.zh: 例如，纳西尔说自己周末查看邮件的频率高得过分。

sentences.en: So, during weekends, she moved the Gmail app from her iPhone’s homepage to the second page.
sentences.zh: 所以，在周末，她把 Gmail 应用从 iPhone 的主屏幕移到了第二屏。

sentences.en: This extra step helped her avoid checking her email.
sentences.zh: 这个额外的步骤帮助她避免查看邮件。

sentences.en: Experts also suggest using an email signature as another tool to manage expectations.
sentences.zh: 专家还建议使用邮件签名作为管理他人期望的另一种工具。

sentences.en: This tool can include more than just your name and contact information.
sentences.zh: 这个工具不仅可以包含你的名字和联系方式。

sentences.en: You can also use it to let others know your working hours or upcoming vacation plans.
sentences.zh: 你也可以用它让别人知道你的工作时间或即将到来的度假计划。

sentences.en: And that’s the Health & Lifestyle report.
sentences.zh: 以上就是健康与生活方式的报道。

sentences.en: And I’m Andrew Smith.
sentences.zh: 我是安德鲁·史密斯。
